newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber seen sinking on baht float.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber seen sinking on baht float.

text.p: The Indonesian rubber market is expected to remain under a cloud in the near term, with Thailand's decision to float its currency adding to the depression, industry sources said on Thursday.
"The outlook is gloomy, at least until September," A.F.S. Budiman, executive director of the Indonesian Rubber Association, which groups producers and traders, told Reuters.
"It will be difficult for prices to go up in July and August because of summer in the industrial countries which will resume their activities in late August or September."
Traders said sustained poor demand coupled with an increase in output had depressed prices from a high of 50.00 cents/lb in April to below 45.00 cents for tyre-grade SIR20.
"What happened in Thailand has affected buyers in the sense that they are using their might to push offer prices down," one trader in Padang, West Sumatra, said by telephone.
"Prices in Thailand will fall due to the baht crisis and we have to follow by cutting prices, whether we like it or not."

Natural rubber futures and cash prices fell sharply in Asia on Wednesday after Thailand, the world's largest producer, floated its currency to pull the country out of an economic slump, prompting the baht to plunge.
Reports in May that the Thai government intervened in the market to prop up prices of RSS3 grade rubber also contributed to the fall in the Indonesian prices, traders said.
Budiman said it was common for prices to fluctuate as they have in Indonesia as the country's rubber market is free whereas Thailand's is subject to government intervention.
"But what happens is such (intervention) becomes a boomerang in Thailand. Prices become cheaper there and levels in Indonesia fall as a result," he said.
"The expectation that the (Thai) intervention will prop up prices has become a contradiction."
The traders said the Thai government's intervention had led to a build-up in stocks in Thailand.
Some traders said prices might improve in Indonesia if the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) intervened in the market.
"Many traders believe that if INRO enters the market due to the current poor prices, such a move will be taken into consideration by traders," one trader said.
"I believe prices will fall further to 40 (U.S.) cents. INRO may enter the market when prices are at such level."
Traders said Indonesia SIR20 was on offer at 43.50 cents/lb fob Palembang for September shipment in early trading on Thursday.
Offer prices were quoted at 44.50 cents fob Belawan, 43.75 cents fob Surabaya, 43.625 cents fob Padang, 43.25 cents fob Pontianak and 43.345 fob Jambi.
